newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UCB drags Brussels bourse lower.
newsitem.headline: UCB drags Brussels bourse lower.

text.p: Chemical and drugs firm UCB dragged the Brussels bourse into the red on Thursday as players sold on Wednesday's news of disappointing first half profits.

"On a gross margin basis (ordinary profit before tax) the results were in line with expectations. But on a net basis, because of the higher tax charge, they have been seen by some people as disappointing," one trader said.
First half current pre-tax profits rose by 33 percent, but as the tax rate rose to 23.5 percent from 18 net results rose only by 24.5 percent.

Traders said that remarks by chief executive officer George Jacobs to the effect that he could not explain the rocket-like performance of the share in recent weeks also served to dampen some of the underlying enthusiasm.
"But you have to bear in mind that it is a very illiquid share, so the movement is exaggerated," one trader said.

At 0845 GMT UCB was 3.6 percent down at 134,200 francs and acting as a lead weight on the blue chip Bel-20 share index which was 0.33 percent or 8.66 points down at 2,587.70. Traders said that because of its Bel-20 weighting of nearly 12 percent UCB's weakness accounted for the bulk of the index fall.
There was little other news to leaven the mood of the Brussels bourse.

Steel cord and wire maker Bekaert was off 300 francs at 27,200 on what traders said was light profit-taking after its recent strong dollar-related performance and the fact that the dollar had eased a bit.
Traders said most were watching to see what oil major PetroFina and chemical firm Solvay would show in their first half reports after the close of business on Thursday.
Generale Bank said in its market commentary it expected PetroFina to report net current profits of 10 billion francs and rated the share a BUY.
The share was unchanged at 15,075 francs at 0900 GMT.
Solvay, which has forecast a slight rise in its first half figures and is renowned for avoiding surprises in its results, was 175 francs up at 23,625.
Generale Bank said it expected the firm to produce a first half net current profit of 6.4 billion francs and rated the share a HOLD.
